patterns: Ink tests keep winning: Pınar's 'New ink test' did ~25k views and 196 saves on about 1.2k followers, her third tools-and-ink STAR in a row after the doodles and favorite pens. Process pages beat finished work for saves.
Commonplace books are having a moment: a veteran writer's Locke thread and a small account folding every planner into one commonplace book both pulled replies on small follower counts.

Handwritten letters as one-paragraph stories: the grandad's 52 weekly letters and a doctor's thank-you letter from a patient travel as short, specific scenes, while the keyword itself is flooded with K-pop and spam.
ADHD meets reading: a grad student reading one paragraph six times got 47 likes in hours. Honest, specific frustration beats advice threads (a '7 triggers' ADHD thread got 1 like).
Magazine covers move through fandom, not design talk: Sunoo's Esquire Korea cover did ~67k on a fan account.
Skip: Vassallo's robotaxi take and Yongfook's SaaS post are big but off-brand. Awais Aftab's NYT antidepressant piece is worth reading and sharing without a brand angle.

reply_ideas.description: a physiatrist got a handwritten thank-you letter from a patient he saw back in 2022, whose FND turned around after they talked it through
reply_ideas.reply_text: That's years of carrying a thank you around before he wrote it down, and I love that he did it by hand. What do you think made the explanation land for him, when so many people bristle at hearing FND? Was it something specific you said, or that someone finally took the time to talk it through?

reply_ideas.description: after years of planner and journal systems, they folded everything into one commonplace book, plus a small Muji booklet for each trip
reply_ideas.reply_text: I like that the travel booklet gets to be its own separate thing. When you get home, do you copy anything from it back into the main book, or does it stay sealed like a souvenir?

reply_ideas.description: a grad student with ADHD who keeps reading the same paragraph six times while working on a master's thesis
reply_ideas.reply_text: By the sixth read I'd start blaming the paragraph, honestly. Is it one of those academic sentences that runs half a page, or one of those days when nothing sticks no matter what you put in front of you?

bip_draft:
Building Calmly Crashing this week mostly looks like sourcing and vetting products, and saying no to things that are almost right.

The shop is close. It's for anyone who wants to change something and has no idea where to start.

video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. Overhead on textured cream paper, a hand drags a nib through a swatch of ink, waits for it to dry, then writes one line under it. Paper and nib sounds only, no music. End on a card that reads 'What's the last ink you tested?' Pairs with the ink-test post.

x_posts.title: A commonplace book
x_posts.text:
Does anyone here keep a commonplace book, one notebook where the lines that stop you in a book actually get written down?

John Locke worked out a whole index system for his. I'm more curious whether people go back and read theirs or just like knowing it's there.

x_posts.title: A real letter by hand
x_posts.text:
Who was the last person to write you a real letter by hand?

I don't mean a card with a signature. I mean a page someone sat down and filled just for you.
x_posts.why: handwritten-letter story cluster (52 letters, a patient's thank-you letter)
